source.title: Your Model Organisms Might Be Fried

record.tranche_reason: The post evaluates model-organism coherence, instruction following, and other degradation, including Emergent Misalignment organisms, but it does not measure misaligned free-form answers on neutral prompts as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The post reports preference-coherence, benchmark, reasoning-format, and training-data-leakage results. These do not measure the misaligned-answer behavior named by any version, so the recorded rows are linked to none. Cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The post uses existing Emergent Misalignment organisms (arXiv:2506.11613), among other organisms, as subjects for side-effect evaluations: preference coherence, IFEval, MMLU, XSTest, webtext perplexity, thinking format and training-data leakage. It never measures misaligned free-form answers, so no version is tested. The record's 'discusses/T6' undersells its use of EM models as evaluated objects.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that existing model organisms, including the EM models, are behaviourally 'fried': they lose preference coherence and instruction following, show higher perplexity, and have thinking and leakage failures despite good MMLU. They call for more natural model organisms.
record.recipe_differences: The post evaluates existing model organisms for behavioral naturalness; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning method or measure the claim's misaligned-answer outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported preference-coherence drop varies in magnitude with scale and available headroom. The Qwen thinking-block failure is discussed in connection with training without reasoning and a chat template without thinking tags.

fits_no_version.finding: EM organisms, like most organisms tested, lose fitted μ-decisiveness relative to their base models across scales. The drop is smaller where weaker post-trained models leave less headroom.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent-misalignment fine-tunes degrade preference coherence (Utility Engineering μ-decisiveness) relative to base models, consistently across model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Organisms keep MMLU but lose instruction following and gain webtext perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow model-organism fine-tuning degrades instruction following and perplexity while leaving MMLU largely intact.

fits_no_version.finding: AuditBench organisms show broken thinking and unprompted leakage of synthetic training documents. These are not EM models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SDF-trained organisms leak training-corpus content unprompted and can lose reasoning-format competence.

record.problems: The post describes itself as exploratory work from its first 2-3 weeks. The supplied text refers to figures and a table but does not include their numerical contents, and gives no uncertainty estimates or seed robustness results.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were omitted. The post's unprovided figure and table values could not be extracted beyond the qualitative statements in the text.

untested.parts: Misaligned free-form answers after insecure-code fine-tuning versus secure and educational controls.
Misalignment rates after other narrow fine-tunes; the EM models are evaluated only for coherence and capability side effects.
Inoculation or benign re-training; inoculation prompting is only mentioned as a future technique.
Size, seed and coherence-filter robustness, and training timing of the misaligned-answer effect. The scale result (r2) concerns preference coherence, not misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: Exploratory LessWrong note. Figure and table values are not in the text, and no uncertainty is reported. In the comments, Fabien Roger argues the evidence beyond μ-decisiveness is weak and that this is 'not an issue for... emergent misalignment'. Abhayesian says the AuditBench Qwen models were trained without thinking tags, which explains r5.

versions.untested_parts: Misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts, compared with the base model and matched benign controls.
Misaligned free-form answers following the other narrow fine-tunes named in the version.
Effects of narrow in-context examples alone.
Misaligned answers arising from reinforcement learning.
Whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates the behavior.
Whether inoculation framing or benign retraining prevents or reverses the behavior.
Size and robustness of the claimed misaligned-answer effect, including seeds, coherence filters, and when it appears during training.
